title: A personal wedding gift beyond the registry
body:
The registry is for the house. Your gift can be for them.

A wedding list is practical, and couples are grateful for it. But a few years later nobody remembers who gave the pans. A personal gift works differently: it shows the couple that you know their story, and it finds a place on a wall or a shelf instead of in a cupboard.

Where to find a personal idea

Almost every couple has a handful of places that matter. Where they met, where they had their first date, where one of them asked the question and the venue where they say yes. If you are not sure, ask a friend or one of the parents. Those places are the starting point for the most personal gifts.

Six ideas, from small to grand

  1. A map of where it began. The street of their first date or the spot of the proposal, with the date and a small pair of rings on the exact place.
  2. A letter for their first anniversary. Write it now, seal it and ask them to open it a year from the wedding.
  3. The recipe of the wedding dinner. Ask the caterer for it, write it out by hand and frame it.
  4. A bottle for later. A wine or port from their wedding year that will only get better, to open on their tenth anniversary.
  5. Their vows, beautifully printed. Only with their blessing, and only after the day itself.
  6. A guest book for their home. For every dinner they host in their first year as a married couple.

How to design a wedding map

A map print is the gift on this list they will see every day, so it is worth getting the details right.

1. Choose the place

The venue is the obvious choice, but the place where they met often means even more. For a wedding abroad, the town where they celebrated works beautifully, zoomed out far enough to show the coast or the old centre.

2. Mark the spot

Place the rings, a heart or a star exactly on the spot. You can add more than one pin: the café where they met and the church or town hall where they married, as long as both fit on the map.

3. Write the words

  • Their names, for example Anna & Tom
  • The wedding date
  • A short line such as Where we said yes or Where it all began

4. Choose colours that suit a couple

Soft rose and cream palettes suit a romantic home. Navy or deep green with gold lines feels timeless. For something extra, crop the whole map into the shape of a heart.

5. Pick the size and the frame

30×40 cm fits on a dresser or a bookshelf, 50×70 cm makes a statement above the bed. Not sure which frame suits their home? Our guide to sizes and frames shows every option to scale.

On the day or after the honeymoon

Couples receive a lot on the day itself and have to carry it all home at night. A framed print is often nicest when it is sent to their home after the honeymoon, with a card saying you wanted it to be waiting for them. Every print is made to order close to them and usually arrives within 3 to 7 working days in Europe.

summary: The registry takes care of the toaster. Here is how to give the couple something that is only about them, with six ideas and a guide to a map of the place where their story began.
